name: Clarithromycin
summary: Macrolide used in H. pylori and MAC regimens and for respiratory infections; notable for potent CYP3A4 inhibition.
mechanism: Binds the 50S ribosomal subunit and inhibits bacterial protein synthesis; active metabolite 14-hydroxyclarithromycin adds activity.
pharmacodynamics: Time-dependent killing with a post-antibiotic effect.

dosing.adult: 250-500 mg PO every 12 hours (respiratory/skin infections; H. pylori regimens)

safety.pregnancy: Avoid — not preferred in pregnancy (animal embryotoxicity)
contraindications: Concurrent QT-prolonging CYP3A4 substrates (e.g. pimozide) or ergot alkaloids
warnings: Potent CYP3A4 inhibition — many drug interactions (statins, colchicine, warfarin)

indications: Sinusitis / acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis
clinicalPearls: Always check CYP3A4 interactions (statins, colchicine, etc.)
Metallic taste is a frequent, benign side effect
good: Reliable oral macrolide for H. pylori and MAC regimens.
bad: CYP3A4 interactions and QT risk; macrolide resistance limits empiric pneumococcal use.
